newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: ZIMBABWE DOLLAR STARTS NEW WEEK SOFTER.
newsitem.headline: ZIMBABWE DOLLAR STARTS NEW WEEK SOFTER.

text.p: The Zimbabwe dollar opened on Monday weaker against hard currencies in fairly quiet interbank trade, foreign exchange dealers said.
"The market is relatively quiet at the moment, though we opened U.S.$16 million short and saw the (exchange) rates firm a little," said one dealer.
"The rates might go up again if there's any major buying and nothing coming in," he added.
Around 0800 GMT, the local unit was at 10.7425/7625 against the U.S. dollar from last Friday's 10.7350/7550 and also eased to 17.8444/8884 from 17.8000/8500 versus sterling.
Against the mark, it was firmer at 6.9173/9333 compared to 6.9600/9800 but was softer on the rand at 2.2702/2768 against 2.2650/2750.
